dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Those auxilia of barbarian stock are spreading over-wrought rumors about those "Lochknights" again.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: I should suggest to Dominus Boethius that we stamp these ridiculous ravings out completely.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And you are...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Hmm? Ah, no need for surprise, citizen. As you see, I am a musician elevated by the Sebastos, yet I am a citizen, just as you are.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Marcia Gordiana Semproniana am I, here by the eminent will of Dominus Boethius to take over from my colleague, Xavierius, and tune the melodies of this land.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Lochknights...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Fret not about the lies those slaves tell. Their so-called Lochknights are but facetious far-fetched fictions.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: They spread rumors and call those barbarians who worship a false god "knights," believing that they shall one day free them from their fated duties.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: I do not condemn such folly, for folly is the way of the lowly. Yet their delusions are fanned ever hotter, such that their melodies are tranquil no longer.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: They must be cured. Once the disturbances here have subsided, I shall act forcefully to correct such strange skeins of supposition.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Delusion and weakness both breed turmoil.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Fare well, citizen. May your slaves be meek, and your song serene.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And you are...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Hmm? Ah! Sorry, I was just thinking about my script, and I started talking to myself...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: I'm Goldoni. I suppose you could consider me a playwright. And as for what I just said... It wasn't anything important. Don't worry about it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the script...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Aye, it's a script for the next film festival.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: To be honest, Xavier, the Furina Award-winning producer from the first festival is my... friend.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: I agreed to his request to write his next script.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: *sigh* If we weren't such long-time acquaintances, I wouldn't have turned down a commission from the Opera Epiclese to write him a script gratis!

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: And he said he'd pay me... Seriously, who does he take me for...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Still, I've only written opera scripts in the past. It wasn't until I started writing that I realized how different writing for films is.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: For example, operas don't usually describe the finer details of a character's movements, but films require you to supply a complete description of the Kamera and visual angles...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, this commission is a brand-new challenge. That's why I'm still trying to decide what the best theme might be...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Farewell. Safe journey!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you an ascended musician, then?

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Indeed, that is so. A flawless body, immortal life, and absolute beauty. Behold, citizen. You look upon the honor bestowed on me by the Sebastos.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: He has caused our bodies to transcend lowly mortality, turning the tragic dirge of death into proud triumph.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: It is by this grace that I have the honor of performing the eternal symphony.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Boethius...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Watch your tone, citizen. Even I do not have the right to address that exalted Dominus solely by his name.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Dominus Boethius is a Harmost, exalted to that post by the Sebastos himself, and is the foremost genius in our empire's history. Even Dominus Cassiodor cannot...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: ...No, forget what I said before. I did not mean to be partisan about our Harmosts.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Regardless, even amongst the empire's outstanding subjects, Dominus Boethius stands tall as the most representative of its spirit.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: His loyalty and passion are undoubtedly worthy of our imitation and respect.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Xavier you mentioned...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Xavierius, citizen, or Lucius Septimius Sebelius. Not "Xavier." Your pronunciation is most strange.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: He was a respectable man, but he put his faith in the wrong thing. Inconceivably, he believed...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: No, he twisted Dominus Cassiodor's words, to the point that he did not notice the barbarians' schemes in time.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Just as you have heard, his negligence caused the fall of Petrocorii. Countless citizens were massacred by the barbarians, and the streets were awash with ruin and blood in a single night.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Weakness only brings calamity, and kindness, disaster. Our ignorant slaves may be swayed by well-meaning lies, but our vision should extend further.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You just said you wanted to write a classic romance story...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: *cough* I—Isn't that very normal? After all, romance and love have been a theatrical theme since time immemorial! I didn't mean anything else, really!

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: As my ancestor... Master Coppelius once said...!

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: "There is no absolute good or evil, only absolute beauty and ugliness. And that which makes beauty is eternal love..."

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Whether it be the chronicle of Chariclea or the legend of the Lochknights, these are all romantic classics...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Wh—Whatever the case, don't misunderstand, you hear?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you Xavier's friend?

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Y... Yes! A—Also, we grew up together. I've known him since I was three!

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: *sigh* If only I knew the first thing about mechanisms. That way, I could've gone with him to Inazuma without anyone batting an eyelid...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Maybe I'd even be able to join his Daydream Club and speak with him more...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: *cough* I mean, I could write more work that suits his requirements. I mean, the more commissions I do for him, the more perfect the scripts I'll write... right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But you look like an ordinary person...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Is that so? Thank you for your praise, citizen. Still, you should direct that adoration to the might and mercy of the Sebastos.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: To carve immortal bodies from stone that look no different from ordinary mortals — who else but he could have achieved this great feat?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Coppelius?

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Yes. Master Coppelius is the greatest playwright in Fontaine's history, and I... am a descendant of his, though my skill is far from comparable to his.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: From "Golden Hyperborea" to "Coppelia" to "Masque of the Great," his works — one and all — rank amongst the greats.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: If only I could be so incandescently artful, I... No, nothing, please, pay it no mind!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sure the producer will like it.

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Thank you. *sigh* If only he would like more than just scripts...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Uh, I—I mean, if only he... if only this would make him like traditional opera more...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: Perhaps we should choose more classical romance for the script this time. The confession of love between Tancrede and Chariclea, perhaps, or the farewell of the Lochknight Drest and Adsiltia...

dialogues.speaker: Goldoni
dialogues.text: *sigh* If only he could understand my intent...
